transcript.text: Can you describe your role as an Engagement Manager leading consulting teams, as mentioned: 'Lead teams of 4-6 consultants on 9-12 week engagements; delivered 11 engagements'?

I have nine years in consulting, the last five as an engagement manager at a global firm. I lead teams of four to six consultants on 9 to 12-week engagements, and I have delivered 11 of them. The one I'm proudest of was a cost-reduction programme for a manufacturing client, where we identified savings of about 14% of addressable spend. I'm applying now because I advise on decisions that someone else carries out, and I want to be the person who carries them out.

You mentioned the cost-reduction programme for a manufacturing client where you identified savings of about 14% of addressable spend. What specific challenges did you face in managing your team and the project to deliver these results?
transcript.anchor_quote: a cost-reduction programme for a manufacturing client, where we identified savings of about 14% of addressable spend

transcript.text: I can't name the client or share the rupee value of the savings. Our engagement letters prohibit that. The 14% figure is already the most I can say about it.

Since you are limited in details you can share about the cost-reduction project, could you describe generally how you ensured your team's coordination and overcame any internal challenges during those engagements?
transcript.anchor_quote: The 14% figure is already the most I can say about it

transcript.text: My leadership style is collaborative and empowering. I focus on creating a high-performance culture and aligning the team towards a common vision, while ensuring client delight.

You mentioned focusing on creating a high-performance culture and aligning the team towards a common vision. Can you share a specific instance where this leadership approach made a measurable impact on your project outcomes?
On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead. A partner designed the whole approach and I only built the spreadsheets.

You mentioned that you built the spreadsheets for the cost reduction programme while a partner designed the approach. Can you tell me about a different project where you took on more leadership responsibility and how you influenced the outcome?
transcript.anchor_quote: On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead. A partner designed the whole approach and I only built the spreadsheets

transcript.text: I'm not sure it is fair to say a consultant has no accountability for results. We are measured on whether the client implements our recommendations. I would rather you ask how I follow through.

feedback.summary: The candidate has extensive consulting experience with a clear aspiration to transition into business leadership. However, they struggled to provide detailed examples of personal ownership and leadership impact, especially on complex projects, due to confidentiality or role limitations. Their explanations about leadership style were general, and they redirected some questions rather than providing the requested specific behavioral examples. There was limited evidence of substantiated outcomes attributable directly to their actions or reflective learning from setbacks.
